adminToken.description: Either a static token from Config.AdminTokens — the right credential for a script, since it has no session and no expiry — or a superuser session token from /api/admin/auth-with-password, which is the right credential for a person. Both arrive the same way and satisfy the same middleware.

ReturnID.name: returnId
ReturnID.description: A return of the order named by id. One belonging to another order is reported as not found.

Offset.name: offset
Offset.description: How many records to skip. Ignored when `page` is also given.

PageNumber.name: page
PageNumber.description: The page to return, counting from 1. An alternative to `offset` — `?limit=20&page=3` is the same window as `?limit=20&offset=40`. When both are sent, `page` wins: it is the more specific intent.

SortOrder.name: order
SortOrder.description: Which way to sort. Only meaningful beside `sort`: sending it alone is refused rather than guessed at, because the default orderings are fixed clauses with their own direction and there is nothing coherent to flip. `desc` is the exact reverse of `asc`, including among rows that tie on the sort field.

From.name: from
From.description: Inclusive lower bound, YYYY-MM-DD or RFC 3339.

ActorID.name: actor_id
ActorID.description: A superuser id. Rows written by a token or by the engine itself carry none and are never matched by this.

DryRun.name: dry_run
DryRun.description: Validate the whole file and roll back.

Lang.name: lang
Lang.description: Overrides Accept-Language. Falls back to the store's default language when unsupported.

ReportFrom.name: from
ReportFrom.description: Inclusive lower bound, YYYY-MM-DD or RFC 3339. A bare date is midnight in `tz`, not in UTC. Defaults to 30 days before `to`, computed in `tz`.

ReportTo.name: to
ReportTo.description: Exclusive upper bound, YYYY-MM-DD or RFC 3339, resolved in `tz`. Defaults to now. Exclusive is the rule GET /api/admin/orders uses, so a range ending on the 30th asks for to=the 1st.

ReportGroupBy.name: group_by
ReportGroupBy.description: The interval each bucket covers. Weeks are ISO, starting Monday. A window of more than 400 buckets at the requested grain is refused, naming a coarser one.

ReportTimeZone.name: tz
ReportTimeZone.description: An IANA zone name whose midnights the buckets and the window bounds are both cut on. Matched case-insensitively against the database's own zone catalogue and echoed back canonicalised.

EventID.name: id
EventID.description: The event's uuid — the stable identity a handler dedupes on and a log line prints, not the table's row number.

Conflict.description: The request conflicts with the current state.

Unauthorized.description: A valid admin token is required.

Forbidden.description: Authenticated, and the role does not carry the right this route needs. Distinct from 401: the credential is good, the answer is still no.

AuthResponse.description: A session token and the operator it belongs to.

Media.description: One file in the store-wide library. Note what is absent: the storage key is an internal handle and is never serialized.

url.description: Where the file is readable. Site-relative for files this store holds.

filename.description: The name it was uploaded under, kept for display only — never used as a path.

OptionChange.description: What replacing the matrix actually did, so an operator is told rather than left to discover it.

values_renamed.description: "Colour: Red → Crimson". Apart from added and removed on purpose: a rename keeps every variant that held the value, and reporting it as a removal plus an addition describes a destruction that did not happen.

variant_ids.description: The variants that show this picture — several when the sizes of one colour share its photographs. Absent for a picture only the product shows.

Superuser.description: An admin-panel operator. Note what is absent: no password hash is ever serialized.

rights.description: What this operator may do, resolved through the store's role matrix. The panel hides what it cannot do from this rather than from a copy of the table.

PasswordResetAccepted.description: The answer to a reset request. `accepted` is always true: the route will not say whether the address belongs to an operator.

delivery.description: How this store delivers a link. `none` means no email backend is installed, nothing will arrive, and no token was written — a fact about configuration, the same for every caller.

PasswordResetTarget.description: Everything a lookup will say about a live link. The account behind it is deliberately not named.

ErrorEnvelope.description: Every failure uses this shape, whatever endpoint produced it.

details.description: Structured detail, such as per-line checkout conflicts.

ListMeta.description: Accompanies every paginated collection. Both coordinate systems are reported: `offset` for a client walking a cursor, and `page` for a UI drawing "3 of 12". The page fields are derived from the offset, so the two can never disagree.

total.description: Matching records in the whole collection, not just this page.

page.description: The page this window falls in, counting from 1.

total_pages.description: Pages at this limit. Zero when nothing matched.

Money.description: An integer count of the currency's minor unit, plus the currency. Never a float, because binary floating point cannot represent 0.10; never a formatted string, because the decimal places belong to the currency and the symbol belongs to the reader's locale.

Product.description: The merchandising concept. What a shopper actually buys is a variant.

product_type.description: Free text an operator groups and filters by, such as "Shirt".

tags.description: Normalised on write: trimmed, de-duplicated case-insensitively, and sorted. Case is preserved, but two spellings of one tag are one tag.

seo_title.description: The storefront's <title>. Empty means derive it from the title — whether and how is the storefront's call.

collections.description: Carried on every product read, so membership renders without a request per product.

metadata.description: Where a module attaches its own data, under its own key.

category.description: Absent when the product is uncategorised, which is a normal state for a draft rather than an error.

ProductOption.description: One axis of choice, such as Size.

Variant.description: The sellable unit: SKU, price and stock live here, and cart and order lines reference it. A product with no options still has exactly one.

stock_on_hand.description: Physically on the shelf, including units promised to open orders. Summed across every location — `GET /api/admin/variants/{id}/stock` is the breakdown.

stock_reserved.description: Promised to orders in flight but not yet taken off the shelf. Summed across every location.

at_location.description: This variant's holding at one place. Present only on the reads that are about a place — a location's stock listing, and the low-stock report for one location. `stock_on_hand` above stays the store-wide sum in the same row; both are true and they answer different questions.

continue_selling.description: Take the order when the count has run out, instead of refusing it.

origin_country.description: Where the item was made, ISO 3166-1 alpha-2.

weight_grams.description: The canonical stored weight. Whole grams, because that is the resolution a carrier API is given and a float that cannot represent 0.1 exactly would eventually produce a total that does not add up.

weight_unit.description: How the weight should be read, exactly as a currency code says how an amount should be read. The grams are the fact; the unit is presentation, kept so an operator who typed 2.5 kg sees 2.5 kg again and not 2500 g.

weight.description: The same mass rendered for display, so a client that only shows it need not know that a pound is 453.59237 g.

images.description: The product's pictures this variant shows, in order — what a storefront swaps to when a shopper picks a colour. Absent for most variants. Several variants may list the same picture.

image.description: The first of `images`, kept as the thumbnail. Absent when the variant shows none, which is the normal case for most variants.

cost.description: What the item cost this store, for margin reporting. Absent means nobody has recorded a cost — which is not the same as a cost of zero, and the difference matters: a zero would report a 100% margin on something nobody has costed. A storefront never sees this.

taxable.description: Whether tax applies to this variant. True for almost everything, and the safe default to be wrong about: tax charged in error is refundable, tax not charged is not. It sits on the variant rather than the product because a gift card and a shirt can share a product's shape and not its tax treatment.

dimensions.description: Absent when nobody has measured the parcel, which is the normal case for most variants.

dimension_unit.description: How the sides should be read, exactly as `weight_unit` says how a mass should be read. The millimetres are the fact; the unit is presentation, kept so an operator who typed 30 cm sees 30 cm again and not 300 mm. One unit covers all three sides, because a box is measured in a single unit by whoever holds the tape.

size.description: The same parcel rendered for display, so a client that only shows it need not know that an inch is 25.4 mm. A side nobody measured reads as an em dash rather than being hidden, so a half-finished parcel says which side is missing.

slug.description: Derived from the title when omitted.

tags.description: Stored normalised — trimmed, de-duplicated case-insensitively and sorted — so the order they arrive in does not become part of the record.

sku.description: Shorthand for a product with no options; send with price_minor instead of variants.

category_id.description: The category to file the product under. Omit for uncategorised.

Collection.description: A named, hand-curated grouping of products. Rule-based ("smart") collections are deliberately absent: they need a query language, and what a catalog this size uses is a list somebody picked.

position.description: Orders collections against each other — a navigation menu, not the order of products inside one.

ProductCollection.description: The trimmed collection carried on a product: enough to render a chip and link to it, and no more.

slug.description: Derived from the title when omitted, exactly as a product's is.

CollectionPage.description: A collection with the active products in it. One request rather than two, because there is no useful moment at which a storefront has the collection but not its contents.

compare_at_price_minor.description: Omitted or null records no compare-at price. On create there is nothing to leave alone, which is why this is not the three-state field the patch has.

options.description: The value chosen on each of the product's axes, in any order.

continue_selling.description: Take the order when the count has run out, instead of refusing it.

origin_country.description: Where the item was made, ISO 3166-1 alpha-2.

weight_grams.description: The weight in grams. The API's shape; a form should send `weight` and `weight_unit` instead.

weight.description: The weight in `weight_unit`, converted server-side. Sent together with the unit this is a form's shape; when both this and `weight_grams` arrive, this one wins — a caller that computed grams itself and then also sent a value contradicted itself, and the human-entered number is the one a person can check.

cost_minor.description: Cost in the store's minor units. Send null to clear a recorded cost.

dimensions.description: The parcel in millimetres. The API's shape; a form should send `size` and `dimension_unit` instead.

dimension_unit.description: How the sides should be read, exactly as `weight_unit` says how a mass should be read. The millimetres are the fact; the unit is presentation, kept so an operator who typed 30 cm sees 30 cm again and not 300 mm. One unit covers all three sides, because a box is measured in a single unit by whoever holds the tape.

id.description: The cart's opaque token, and the only credential involved.

status.description: An expired cart that holds something is now marked `abandoned` rather than deleted, so GET on it answers 200 with this status where it used to 404 - and the next mutation revives it to `open` with a fresh TTL. An expired cart holding nothing is still deleted outright.

price_changed.description: The live price differs from the snapshot, so checkout will refuse until the shopper confirms.

available.description: -1 when the variant does not track inventory.

id.description: The cart's row id. The cart token is deliberately absent: it is the shopper's credential, and possessing it authorises every mutation on the basket.

state.description: What the cart is, derived from status AND expires_at. An `open` cart past its TTL reports `abandoned` before the sweeper reaches it.

updated_at.description: When the shopper last changed the cart. The abandonment sweep deliberately does not touch it.

abandoned_at.description: When the sweeper marked it. Also the retention clock.

payment_data.description: Passed through to the payment provider, so a gateway can receive what it needs without this body growing a field per integration.

return_url.description: Where a redirect-flow gateway sends the shopper back to.

metadata.description: A `notes` key is refused with a 400: it is reserved for the shop's own note on the order, which is set through PATCH /api/admin/orders/{id}.

kind.description: `none` means nothing further is needed — cash on delivery.

Order.description: An immutable record of a sale. Its lines and customer details are snapshots, so a historical order stays readable after the catalog moves on.

status.description: partial means some of what was ordered has gone out and some has not; shipped still means all of it. It is derived from the shipments and never set directly.

refunded.description: What has gone back to the customer. payment_status stays paid while any of the money is still the store's, and becomes refunded only once this reaches the total.

refunds.description: Every refund on this order, oldest first.

returns.description: What has come back off this order, oldest first, including returns that were later withdrawn. Empty on a guest's copy: it is the store's operational record rather than a fact about what the shopper bought.

metadata.description: Where a module attaches its own data, under its own key. The reserved key `notes` is the shop's own note on the order and is absent from GET /api/orders/{number}.

access_token.description: How a guest reads their own order back. Returned at checkout and by POST /api/admin/orders/{id}/access-token; absent from every order read, guest or admin.

shipped_quantity.description: How many of this line have gone out, summed across the order's shipments. Derived on the way out, never stored.

returned_quantity.description: How many of this line have come back on returns that still stand. Summed on the way out, never stored, and absent when nothing has.

location_id.description: Where these units were taken from, decided once at checkout so that cancelling puts them back on the shelf they left. Absent on a line placed before locations existed, or one whose location has since been closed.

carrier.description: Who is carrying the parcel, as a carrier code. A different fact from the provider that booked it.

carrier_name.description: The carrier's display name, derived from its code on the way out.

tracking_url.description: Where to follow the parcel, derived from the carrier and the number on the way out and never stored.

lines.description: What went in this parcel. Empty on a shipment recorded before shipments named their contents.

Refund.description: One movement of money back to the customer. A guest reading their own order with its access token sees only refunds that actually moved money, and without reason, by or error — those belong to the operator.

status.description: pending only while the provider is being asked: the row is committed before that call, and is what stops a second refund spending the same money.

provider.description: The method the money went out through, as it was at the time.

provider_reference.description: The gateway's own id for the refund — what a bank statement is reconciled against. Empty when the provider does not report one.

error.description: What the provider said when it refused.

by.description: The operator's email as it was then. Empty when a script holding the static admin token did it.

OrderReturn.description: Goods that came back off an order. It moves no money: refundable is what the goods were worth — unit price times quantity, less the line's share of the order discount, plus its share of the tax where prices exclude it — and is a suggestion for whoever decides about a refund, never a settlement.

status.description: withdrawn means the record was taken back and the units it put on the shelf came off again. Only a received return counts against what may still come back.

units.description: How many units came back, summed from the lines on the way out.

restocked_units.description: How many of them went back on sale. Less than units whenever something came back damaged.

refundable.description: What the goods were worth. NOT a refund amount: no money moved on this record.

OrderReturnLine.description: How much of one order line came back. The sku, title and label are joined in on the way out, because the row itself stores an id and a count.

restocked.description: Whether these units went back on sale. It records what happened rather than what was asked: a line whose variant has since been deleted stores false, because there is no shelf left to put it back on.

location_id.description: The shelf they went back on. Absent when nothing moved.

refundable.description: What these units were worth, snapshotted when the return was recorded.

FulfillmentLine.description: How much of one order line went in one parcel. The sku, title and label are joined in on the way out, because the row itself stores an id and a count.

Category.description: A node in the product taxonomy. Not a collection: a collection is a curated list a product can be on six of, while a category answers "what kind of thing is this", which has exactly one answer — which is what a feed, a tax rule and a shipping profile all need to key off.

position.description: Orders a category against its siblings.

full_name.description: The ancestry joined for display. Computed on read, never stored: a stored path would need rewriting across a whole subtree on every rename, and the first missed rewrite is a lie nothing ever finds.

depth.description: 0 for a root. Present so a flat listing can be indented without the client rebuilding the tree.

children.description: Populated by the nested listing only. A flat listing omits it, so the same rows never appear twice in one response.

metadata.description: The `attributes` key is the list of fields this category asks of a product, as `{key, label}`. A choice list written here is ignored on read — the dictionary at /api/admin/taxonomy-attributes is where a field's values live.

attributes.description: The fields this category asks of a product: its own declarations out of metadata, with the choices the shared dictionary holds for each handle. Populated by the ancestors route only.

CategoryAttribute.description: One field a category asks of a product. `key` and `label` are the category's own, out of its metadata; `choices` comes from the shared dictionary and is empty for a handle nobody has defined, which is a free-text field rather than a broken one.

TaxonomyImport.description: Created counts rows written; matched counts categories that were already in the right place and were left alone, which is what makes a second run a no-op.

TaxonomyAttributeImport.description: Unmatched counts lines naming a category this store does not have, which is the ordinary case when the tree came from a different release or only part of it was kept.

attributes.description: Absent for an uploaded file: the field definitions match on a taxonomy id only the embedded tree writes, so nothing was attempted and a report of zeros would read like a failure.

ProductCategory.description: The trimmed category carried on a product: enough to render a breadcrumb and link to it.

slug.description: Derived from the title when absent.

parent_id.description: Null files the category at the root. The tree is capped at 8 deep.

metadata.description: The `attributes` key is the list of fields this category asks of a product, as `{key, label}`, inherited by everything beneath it. A `choices` list written here is ignored on read — the dictionary at /api/admin/taxonomy-attributes is where a field's values live, keyed by the same handle.

CategoryPage.description: A category with the active products filed under it or under anything beneath it. Descendants are included because that is what the operator means: someone who picks "Apparel" wants the shirts too.

VariantImage.description: One of its product's pictures a variant shows — what a storefront swaps to when a shopper picks a colour. A variant never owns a file; it points at ones the product already shows, so the same picture is stored once however many sizes share it.

CategoryPatch.description: Only the keys present are written. Moving a category re-parents its whole subtree, so the depth cap and the cycle check apply to the move.

slug.description: Derived from the title when absent.

parent_id.description: Null files the category at the root. The tree is capped at 8 deep.

metadata.description: The `attributes` key is the list of fields this category asks of a product, as `{key, label, choices}`, inherited by everything beneath it. A `choices` list written here is ignored on read; the dictionary holds a field's values.

track_url.description: Where the customer follows the parcel, with the number already in it. Absent when the carrier has no URL that takes the number as a parameter — a client should then show the number without a link rather than a link that fails.

FulfillmentPatch.description: Only the keys present are written. Changing the tracking number re-identifies the carrier, because the stored one described the old number; an explicit `carrier` in the same request wins over that.

carrier.description: A code from GET /api/admin/carriers, or empty.

OrderPatch.description:
Corrects what was recorded about an order: who it is for, and how it was paid for. Only the keys present are written.

It deliberately cannot reach status, payment status, totals or line items. Each of those is a state change with consequences — stock, events, money — and each already has an operation that performs them properly. This is for the fields somebody typed.

email.description: Required to be non-empty: it is how the customer hears about the order.

payment_provider.description: A method installed in this build. It may be changed while nothing has been refunded — an order taken as cash on delivery and actually settled by transfer should say so — but not after, where the money went out through the provider currently on the order.

payment_reference.description: The transaction or receipt number the money is reconciled against.

metadata.description: Replaced whole, not merged: send the keys you want the order to end up with. The reserved key `notes` is the operator's note on this order — it must be a string, it is absent from the shopper's own read of the order, and it cannot be set at checkout. A patch that carries only `metadata` and changes nothing but `notes` emits no event and is accepted on a cancelled order, because a note is not a state change; a metadata patch that also alters another key is an ordinary edit and announces itself.

balance_minor.description: What the edit moved the total by: positive is owed by the customer, negative is owed to them.

OrderChange.description: What an edit did to an order's lines, and the totals either side of it. Also carried by an `order.edited` event and by the `change` on that event's timeline entry.

OrderTimelineEntry.description: One thing that happened to an order, merged from the outbox and the audit trail. A transition caused by an operator writes into both in one transaction and renders here once, carrying the actor from the trail and the delivery state from the outbox.

kind.description: `action` where somebody was recorded doing this, `event` where all that survives is the announcement — a transition from before the trail existed, or one whose record names no event.

name.description: The event this announced, absent where it announced nothing. Writing a note is the one order write that is deliberately quiet.

action.description: The operator's verb, absent on an entry with no audit row behind it. Deliberately not the event name: `order.edit_lines` and `order.update` both announce `order.edited`.

summary.description: What the act was, in a sentence.

actor_kind.description: A person, a script holding a static admin token, or the engine's own background work.

actor_email.description: The operator's email as it was then. Absent for a token and for the system — a credential is not a person.

actor_role.description: The role they held at the time, which may not be the one they hold now.

actor_label.description: A name for a caller that is not a person: a sweeper, a cron job, a module.

event_id.description: The event's own id, stable across redeliveries.

published_at.description: When every subscribed handler accepted it. Absent means it is still queued — or, with `dead`, that nobody could be told at all.

attempts.description: Delivery attempts so far. Absent means none.

dead.description: The engine has given up delivering it.

last_error.description: What the failing handler said. Returned only to a caller holding `store.operate`, and absent otherwise: it is a raw error string and can carry an upstream URL or a fragment of a key.

status.description: The order's status as the event left it.

before.description: The fields this act moved, as they were. Money keys are the same `*_minor` integers the API uses. Absent means the previous value was not recorded, never that it was empty.

after.description: The same fields, as they became.

Discount.description: A rule an operator maintains. What an order was actually given is a separate snapshot — see AppliedDiscount — so a promotion that has ended may be deleted without rewriting history.

code.description: What a shopper types. Matched case-insensitively and unique that way. Absent means automatic, which is reserved and not evaluated at checkout yet.

value_bp.description: Basis points for a percentage: 1000 is 10.00%. An integer, because a percentage of money is money-adjacent and floats are forbidden near it.

value_minor.description: The amount for a fixed discount, in minor units.

scope.description: What the rule comes off. `order` is the whole basket. `products`, `collections` and `categories` mean the value comes off only the lines whose product is named by `target_ids` — directly, by collection membership read at checkout, or by category, which reaches the whole subtree beneath the categories named. A basket holding none of them is refused the code. `free_shipping` cannot be scoped: shipping is not part of any line.

target_ids.description: What a scoped rule points at: product, collection or category ids according to `scope`. Absent for an order-wide rule. Returned by both the listing and the single read, so a client editing a rule holds the whole set without a second request.

targets.description: The same targets resolved for a reader. Returned by GET /api/admin/discounts/{id} only — a listing returns ids, because a rule aimed at two hundred products would otherwise put two hundred titles into a page of fifty rows.

min_subtotal_minor.description: The basket this needs before it applies, measured on the whole basket even for a scoped rule: it is the price of entry to a promotion, not the thing discounted. Absent is no minimum, which is not the same as zero.

used_count.description: Read-only: a fact about what happened, not a setting.

once_per_email.description: Per email, not per customer, and named so. Guest checkout is permanent (D22), so there is no customer to count against — this is a deterrent, not a control.

DiscountTarget.description: One thing a scoped discount points at, resolved for a reader.

kind.description: Singular, against `scope`'s plural: a scope describes a rule, a kind describes one row. It is derived from the scope and never sent.

title.description: Read-only. A category's is its full ancestry ("Apparel / Shirts"), because the leaf alone does not say which one.

missing.description: The catalog row is gone. The target is kept rather than cleaned up, so a promotion that has narrowed is visible rather than silent.

AppliedDiscount.description: What a basket was given: the snapshot an order keeps forever.

discount_id.description: 0 once the rule that produced it has been deleted.

code.description: What a shopper types. Matched case-insensitively and unique that way. Absent means automatic, which is reserved and not evaluated at checkout yet.

value_bp.description: Basis points for a percentage: 1000 is 10.00%. An integer, because a percentage of money is money-adjacent and floats are forbidden near it.

value_minor.description: The amount for a fixed discount, in minor units.

scope.description: What the rule comes off. `order` is the whole basket. `products`, `collections` and `categories` mean the value comes off only the lines whose product is named by `target_ids` — directly, by collection membership read at checkout, or by category, which reaches the whole subtree beneath the categories named. A basket holding none of them is refused the code. `free_shipping` cannot be scoped: shipping is not part of any line.

target_ids.description: What the rule points at: product, collection or category ids according to `scope` — the kind is never sent, because the scope decides it. Required and non-empty for `products`, `collections` and `categories`; absent or empty for `order` and for an omitted scope. Duplicates are deduped and order is not stored. On PATCH: absent leaves the stored set alone, a list replaces it whole, and `[]` clears it, which is legal only when the resulting scope is `order`.

min_subtotal_minor.description: The basket this needs before it applies, measured on the whole basket even for a scoped rule: it is the price of entry to a promotion, not the thing discounted. Absent is no minimum, which is not the same as zero.

usage_limit.description: How many times the code may be redeemed in total. Absent leaves a stored limit alone; an explicit null removes it, so a promotion can be reopened without recreating it. Zero is refused: a limit of none is null, not 0.

once_per_email.description: Per email, not per customer, and named so. Guest checkout is permanent (D22), so there is no customer to count against — this is a deterrent, not a control.

TaxRate.description: A rule about a place and a kind of thing. The most specific rule that fits a line is the one that applies: a category beats a country, a country beats a bare fallback, and within categories the deeper one wins. A rule on a category reaches its whole subtree.

name.description: What appears on the invoice, e.g. "GST 18%".

rate_bp.description: Basis points: 1800 is 18.00%. An integer, like every other money-adjacent figure here.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2. Empty is the fallback every other rule is more specific than.

name.description: What appears on the invoice, e.g. "GST 18%".

rate_bp.description: Basis points: 1800 is 18.00%. An integer, like every other money-adjacent figure here.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2. Empty is the fallback every other rule is more specific than.

Location.description: A place stock physically is: a shop, a warehouse, a shelf in somebody's garage. Every store has one from the day it is created, and a store with a single location never has to name it — every stock operation defaults to it.

code.description: Stable, lowercase and unique. What an import or a script refers to.

priority.description: Lower is preferred. A reservation is taken from the first active location, in this order, that can cover the quantity.

active.description: Whether new orders may be filled from here. A location holding stock cannot be deactivated: move the stock first.

is_default.description: Where stock lands when nothing names a place. Exactly one location has this.

on_hand.description: Units held here, across every variant.

skus.description: How many variants have a non-zero count here.

StockMovement.description: One row of the append-only stock ledger. Two deltas rather than one, because a commit takes units out of the reservation and off the shelf in the same movement and a single signed number could not say which happened. Every row records what the statement APPLIED, never what the caller asked for — five of the writers move nothing for a variant that does not track inventory, one floors a release at zero, and two write absolutely — which is what makes sum(on_hand_delta) reconcile to on_hand for every (variant, location) pair. variant_id and location_id go null when their parent is deleted, while sku and location_code keep what the row was written with, so history survives a deleted SKU and a closed shelf. A null superuser_id means no person was behind it; `source` then names which path was.

variant_id.description: Null once the variant has been deleted; `sku` still names it.

location_id.description: Null once the location has been deleted; `location_code` still names it.

source.description: Which path moved the stock, not who: whether a person or a static admin token was behind an `admin` movement is superuser_id's job. `migration` belongs to the ledger's own opening balances.

reason.description: The operator's own words, when they gave any.

counterpart_location_id.description: The other end of a transfer.

superuser_id.description: Null when no person was behind the movement — a checkout, the unpaid sweeper, a script holding a static token — or when the operator's account has since been deleted, in which case actor_email still names them.

VariantStock.description: One variant's holding at one location. Every location is listed, including those holding none of it — that is where a transfer would be sent.

active.description: Whether this location can fill orders.

Invitation.description: An invitation to join the team. The alternative it replaces is an owner inventing somebody else's password and then telling it to them, which means two people know it from the moment it exists.

rights.description: What the role carries. Sent so the person deciding to invite can see what they are handing over.

token.description: The secret, present on the creating response and never again — only its SHA-256 is stored. Losing it means issuing a new invitation.

accept_url.description: The link to send, built from the request so it resolves from wherever the store is actually reached. Present with `token` and just as briefly.

invited_by.description: The inviter's email. Empty when the static admin token issued it, which has no person behind it.

status.description: Expiry is a fact about now rather than a column, so it is resolved on the way out.

RoleSet.description: What one role may do in this store, beside what the engine ships for it. A role with no stored override keeps tracking the default, so a right added to a role in a later release reaches every store that never re-cut it.

rights.description: The effective set: what this role may do here.

default.description: What the engine ships for this role, and what a reset returns to.

customized.description: Whether this store has departed from the default.

configurable.description: False for owner, which always carries every right: it is the way back into a store that has been configured into a corner, so it is not storable.

RoleMatrix.description: The whole permission model in one response, so a client renders the grid without keeping its own copy of either axis.

all_rights.description: The closed catalogue of rights, in display order.

required.description: What no role can be stripped of. A role without catalog.read can sign in and see nothing, which is a removed operator rather than a narrower one.

created_at.description: The transaction's start time. An audit row and the outbox event written by the same transaction therefore carry an identical instant, because now() is transaction_timestamp().

actor_kind.description: A person, a script holding a static admin token, or the engine itself. The three are different facts: a trail that cannot tell a deploy script from the unpaid sweeper answers a different question from the one it was asked.

actor_id.description: Null for a token and for the system. It may point at a superuser who has since been deleted: who did it is a fact about the past and outlives the account.

actor_email.description: The email as it was at the time, snapshotted rather than joined.

actor_role.description: The role as it was at the time. Somebody who is a manager today may have been staff when they did this.

actor_label.description: A name for a caller that is not a person, such as the unpaid sweeper. Never the token.

action.description: What was done, as <record>.<verb>. These are not event names: order.edit_lines and order.update both publish order.edited, and order.refund publishes nothing at all.

entity_id.description: Text, because not everything an operator changes is numbered: a role is "manager".

entity_label.description: What the record was called at the time, kept so the log stays readable after it is renamed and after it is deleted.

changes.description: A key present in after and absent from before means the previous value was not recorded, never that it was empty. Money is always an integer *_minor key plus a currency, never a formatted string.

event.description: The outbox event the same transaction published, where there was one. It is what lets a timeline drawn from both tables render each fact once.

AuditActor.description: Somebody who appears in the trail. Built from the trail and never from the team table, so it does not hand the roster to a reader who holds store.operate but not team.read.

StoreSettings.description: What this store is configured as. A hand-written whitelist over the engine's configuration rather than a dump of it: the configuration also holds the database URL and the admin tokens, so a field appears here because somebody decided it should.

version.description: The engine version this store is running.

currency.description: The store's single settlement currency, as an ISO 4217 code.

default_language.description: The BCP 47 tag used when a request expresses no preference.

languages.description: Every tag this store serves. The default language is always one of them. Empty is impossible, and it is an array rather than null so a client can iterate it without a guard.

prices_include_tax.description: True when every catalog price is gross — the tax is already inside the figure — rather than net with tax added at checkout. It is snapshotted onto each order as it is placed, so changing it never rewrites what last month's orders were saying.

flat_shipping.description: Added to every order. It is the whole of the built-in shipping calculation; a rate engine is a module's job.

cart_ttl_seconds.description: How long an untouched cart survives before the sweeper deletes it, in seconds.

order_ttl_seconds.description: How long an unpaid order holds its inventory reservation before it is cancelled and the stock released, in seconds.

media_uploads_enabled.description: False when this store has nowhere to put files. The media library still records files by URL, so a client should say why the upload button is missing rather than hide the library.

payment_methods.description: The payment methods this binary was composed with, sorted by code.

fulfillment_providers.description: The shipping backends this binary was composed with, sorted by code.

modules.description: The modules this binary was composed with, named, in the order they were passed to New — the order their migrations ran in. Names and nothing else: a client's question is "was this binary built with cms", and anything richer would describe the running process rather than the store's configuration. Empty in a binary built with no modules.

notifier_channels.description: Every notification channel the engine has, whether or not anything is behind it — a channel with no backend still appears, because "sms is not configured" is an answer and a missing row is not. Read `delivers` before anything else: with no vendor module installed the engine's built-in logger writes the message to the process log and reports success, so sending appears to work and nobody receives anything.

NotifierChannelInfo.description: One notification channel and what stands behind it.

channel.description: The channel. The set is closed in v1 because the dispatcher has to know which recipient field feeds a channel.

delivers.description: True when at least one backend on this channel is not the built-in logger. False is the trap: the send succeeds, the outbox marks the event delivered, and the message reached nobody.

backends.description: The registered backends, in registration order. Notifiers append rather than replace, so a store may send an email and mirror it to an audit sink.

NotifierBackend.description: One delivery backend registered on a channel.

name.description: What the backend calls itself when it offers a name, the module that registered it otherwise, and "log" for the built-in logger. A notifier has no code the way a payment provider does — nothing addresses one by name — so there is nothing more canonical to fall back to.

module.description: Which module registered it. "core" is the built-in logger.

delivers.description: False for the built-in logger, which writes one line and returns success.

ProviderInfo.description: An installed provider, as an operator should see it.

code.description: What the API speaks: the code in the checkout URL and on the order.

name.description: The label to show a person. Falls back to the code when the provider offers no name, because the module that installs a provider is the only thing that knows what it is called.

module.description: Which module installed it. "core" is a built-in.

redeemed_total.description: What this promotion has given away, cancelled orders excluded, in the store's settlement currency. Not `used_count`: that is the claim made at checkout and is never given back, so the two are allowed to disagree.

redeemed_orders.description: Live orders carrying a redemption of this rule in the store's currency.

redeemed_other_currency_orders.description: Live redemptions on orders in some other currency, which `redeemed_total` therefore leaves out. Zero in a store that has never changed currency.

DiscountDetail.description: The rule plus what it has cost. Returned by the detail route only.

DiscountRedemption.description: One order that used a rule. The code and title are the snapshot taken at checkout, not the rule's current ones, so a promotion that has since been renamed still reads as what it was.

amount.description: What this order was given, in the order's own currency.

order_total.description: The order's total, in its own currency.

DiscountPreview.description: The answer to "would this work". A refusal is data here and an error on the public cart route; the difference is the question, not the rule.

applied.description: Present when `applies` is true. A free-shipping rule carries `free_shipping: true` and `amount_minor: 0`.

reason.description: Present when `applies` is false — the engine's own sentence, e.g. "that discount has expired", "that discount has been fully used", "automatic discounts are not applied at checkout yet".

sessions.description: Live sessions this operator holds right now.

newest_session.description: When the newest live session started — not a last sign-in. Expired sessions are deleted, so null means nobody is signed in now, never that they have never signed in.

SuperuserRow.description: One operator as the team listing needs them: the record, plus what only a listing asks.

SalesSubset.description: One slice of the sale set, cut by payment status.

PaidSales.description: The settled slice. Partiality is a number and not a status (D36), so an order that has had some of its money sent back is still `paid` and its whole total is here — `refunded` and `net_collected` are what say how much of it the store still holds.

refunded.description: refunded_minor summed over exactly these orders: money that has gone back out of orders still recorded as paid.

net_collected.description: total less refunded — what the store actually still holds.

ExcludedSales.description: Placed in the window and not a sale: still in checkout, or cancelled. Reported beside the totals and never inside them, so a figure that disagrees with the Orders list can be explained.

SalesBucket.description: One calendar day, ISO week or month of the window, cut in `time_zone`.

end.description: Exclusive, and exactly the next bucket's start.

partial.description: The window clips this bucket, so its figures cover less than a whole day, week or month. What stops "sales are down today" being read off three hours of trading.

units.description: Line quantities summed over the same orders.

items.description: subtotal_minor summed: what the goods were priced at, before any discount.

tax.description: Tax on the order, whether the prices contained it or not.

net.description: items less discount, and less tax when the order's prices contained it — so `total = net + tax + shipping` holds under either tax mode. Refunds are never netted off it.

total.description: total_minor summed: what the customer was charged.

refunded.description: Orders whose every minor unit has come back, so `payment_status` reads refunded. Counted and reported, never netted off `net` — and the money behind a partial refund is in `paid.refunded` instead.

SalesTotals.description: The window, added up from its own buckets — never queried a second time, so a stat card and the chart beneath it cannot disagree.

items.description: subtotal_minor summed: what the goods were priced at, before any discount.

tax.description: Tax on the order, whether the prices contained it or not.

net.description: items less discount, and less tax when the order's prices contained it — so `total = net + tax + shipping` holds under either tax mode. Refunds are never netted off it.

total.description: total_minor summed: what the customer was charged.

average_order.description: total / orders, rounded half up: an average in minor units has no fractional part the ledger could show. Zero when nothing sold.

CurrencySales.description: One currency's figures. Orders snapshot their currency (D14), so a store that changed it has more than one block — and minor units of two currencies are never added together.

time_zone.description: The zone the buckets and the window edges were both cut in, canonicalised.

currencies.description: One block per currency the window contains, plus the store's configured currency even when it sold nothing. The store's own currency is first; the rest follow alphabetically. Nothing is ever summed across blocks.

ProductSales.description: One product or variant over the window. Title, SKU and label are the newest snapshot the order lines carry, so a renamed or deleted product still reports under a name somebody recognises.

product_id.description: Null once the product has been deleted; the row stays, and two deleted products stay two rows.

revenue.description: Line value excluding tax under either tax mode, and BEFORE any order-level discount: a discount is recorded once per order and never allocated to lines, so these rows exceed the sales report's `net` by exactly the discounts in the window.

OutboxEvent.description: One row of the transactional outbox: the delivery facts around an event, not the event as a handler received it — hence `payload` rather than `data`.

seq.description: The table's row number. Ordering only — the list sorts on it because it is the dispatcher's own ordering key. An event's identity is `id`.

id.description: The event uuid, which is what every route here takes and every log line prints.

state.description: Derived. `published` wins over `dead`: a row can hold both flags when a slow batch outlives its visibility window, and the delivery is the fact that matters.

attempts.description: Incremented on claim. At 12 the row is parked dead. A retry resets it only on a dead row.

last_error.description: Why the last attempt failed. A retry does not clear it — the diagnosis outlives the repair.

available_at.description: When the dispatcher may next take it. In the future means either backed off or claimed by a worker; nothing in the row tells those apart.

payload.description: Omitted from list responses; returned by the detail route.

requeued.description: How many dead letters this call moved back to pending. Capped at 500.

remaining.description: Dead letters still parked after this call, counted in the same transaction. Non-zero means click again.

DiagnosticReport.description: One run of every check, in the engine's own order. `ok` is false when any check failed, which is the same condition `gocommerce doctor` exits non-zero on — warnings do not flip it, because a busy healthy store routinely carries some.

version.description: The engine version that produced the report.

Diagnostic.description: One check's verdict. The underlying database error behind a check that could not run is deliberately absent: the engine records it separately and the API withholds it, so it is in the store's log rather than in this response.

name.description: Stable, and part of the contract: clients key behaviour to these names.

detail.description: What the check found, in a sentence.

hint.description: What to do about it. Every failing check carries one; a passing check does not.

countries.description: ISO country codes. Empty means anywhere.

states.description: ISO state codes. Empty means anywhere within the countries above.

name.description: What the shopper sees, such as Standard or Express.

rate_id.description: Send this back as shipping_rate_id on checkout.

Dimensions.description: A parcel's three sides in whole millimetres — the canonical stored value, exactly as `weight_grams` is for the mass beside it. An absent side is one nobody has measured, which is not a side of zero: a zero-height parcel is a carrier error, an unmeasured one is paperwork still to do.

DimensionValues.description: The same three sides as a person typed them, in `dimension_unit`, converted server-side. Sent together with the unit this is a form's shape; sending `dimensions` is the API's. When both name a side this one wins — a caller that computed millimetres itself and then also sent a value contradicted itself, and the human-entered number is the one a person can check. The rule `weight` follows against `weight_grams`.

DimensionPatch.description: A parcel's three sides as a patch, in `dimension_unit`. A side left out is kept; an explicit null clears it back to unmeasured; a number sets it. The three states are the point: emptying a box and never touching it are different intentions, and storing zero for the first would tell a carrier the parcel is flat.

code.description: The stable handle a script or an import names the group by, so a renamed group stays the same group.

members.description: How many addresses are in it.

group_id.description: Absent is everybody — a launch price, a seasonal one. It does not mean nobody.

priority.description: Breaks a tie when two live lists both cover a line. Higher wins.

prices.description: How many rows the list holds.

channel_id.description: Absent is every channel, for the same reason an absent group is everybody.
Narrow the list to one storefront. Null is every channel.

min_quantity.description: The quantity break. 1 is any quantity, and is what an absent field means.

amount_minor.description: The unit price in the store's currency's minor units, like every other amount here.

code.description: What a storefront names itself as, in `?channel=` or the `X-Channel` header.

active.description: An inactive channel refuses requests rather than answering with an empty catalogue, which would read as a broken import.

default.description: The channel a request naming none is served from. Exactly one carries it, enforced by a partial unique index — two defaults is a state with no meaning.

products.description: How many products have been narrowed to it. Not how many it sells: a product narrowed to no channel at all sells on every one.

default.description: Setting this moves the default rather than adding a second one.

Screen.description: A screen a module contributes to the admin panel, described as data rather than shipped as code — the panel is compiled once and embedded, so a module cannot put components into it.

slug.description: The URL segment the panel serves it at, under /x/. Unique across modules; the engine refuses a collision at boot.

module.description: Stamped by the engine, so a descriptor cannot claim to come from somewhere it does not.

icon.description: A Remix Icon class, the set the panel already ships.

group.description: The settings-sidebar heading it appears under. Empty puts it under the module's own name.

right.description: The right that gates both the nav entry and the screen. Required — a screen with no right would be visible to everyone with a session.

empty.description: What the table says with no rows. A sentence about this screen rather than "No data".

key.description: A field of the row. Dots reach into nested objects.

kind.description: How the cell is drawn. An unknown kind falls back to text, so a module built against a newer engine degrades rather than breaking.

form.description: Optional. Without it the screen is a reading.

update.description: A PATCH endpoint with {id} where the row's id goes.

delete_warning.description: The sentence in the confirm dialog. A module knows what deleting one of its rows costs and the panel does not.
